communications.subject: Vermont Public Records Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Vermont Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: FBI: Port of Seattle Commissioner Patricia "Pat" Davis

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: Port of Seattle Commissioner Patricia "Pat" Davis
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of all records maintained by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including FBI Headquarters and the Seattle Field Office (and its resident agencies), that reference or pertain to:

Patricia “Pat” Davis (also searched as Patricia Davis and Pat Davis)
DOB: June 27, 1935 | DOD: October 3, 2026
Seattle, Washington; Port of Seattle Commissioner, 1985–2009

Proof of death and privacy
Ms. Davis died on October 3, 2026, at age 91. The Privacy Act protects only living individuals, so no consent is required. Death is documented by:

The Seattle Times obituary: https://obituaries.seattletimes.com/obituary/patricia-pat-davis-1094095687
The Port of Seattle statement: https://www.portseattle.org/news/statement-port-seattle-passing-former-commissioner-pat-davis

I ask that the FBI weigh Exemptions 6 and 7(C) in light of her death and her role as a long-serving elected public official, and the public interest in how federal agencies interacted with her in that role.

Search scope:

Please search the Central Records System (main files and cross-references), Sentinel and legacy ACS indices, and ELSUR indices, using name variants, at FBIHQ and the Seattle Field Office. Please use any available electronic search capability beyond the indices, and tell me if you determine it is not feasible.

Subjects and timeframes

1999 WTO Ministerial (January 1, 1998 – December 31, 2000). Records in which Ms. Davis is a subject, liaison contact, or named participant, including correspondence, meeting notes, threat assessments, briefings, and post-event reviews. This includes any role with the Seattle Bid Committee, the Seattle Host Organization, or the WTO Public Safety Executive Committee. It specifically includes communications between Ms. Davis and Special Agent in Charge Charles “Charlie” Mandigo, and between Ms. Davis and whoever served as Seattle SAC before his arrival, as well as ASACs or WTO command-post staff.

Port of Seattle contracting audit and federal inquiry (January 1, 2007 – December 31, 2010). Records referencing Ms. Davis in connection with the federal inquiry that followed the December 2007 State Auditor’s report on Port contracting, including third-runway contracts. This covers FD-302s, interview summaries, referral and opening/closing memoranda, and liaison with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and DOT-OIG. It also covers any complaint, referral, or inquiry concerning the 2007 Dinsmore severance memo. I do not seek material protected by Fed. R. Crim. P. 6(e), but I request release of all non-grand-jury records.

Post-9/11 port security (September 11, 2001 – December 31, 2009). Records naming Ms. Davis in FBI liaison, threat briefings, or infrastructure-protection contacts with the Port of Seattle, including seaport security matters. If JTTF records are involved, include them only where she is named.

Any other file. Any record naming Ms. Davis regardless of subject (for example, mid-1990s labor-racketeering matters), through the date of search. 

According to a blog post I just read, it is important that I state the following: "As you know, your agency is required to search the records stored at NARA’s Washington Records Center in Suitland, MD, but still technically under your agency’s control. For more information see 36 CFR 1250.8" Please also conduct a physical search of records at NARA's Washington Records Center in Suitland, for any records or documents related to Patricia "Pat" Davis. If related records have been transferred to NARA, then please list them. 

If the bureau cannot fulfill certain parts of this request or if certain portions must be redacted, please provide any reasonable segregable portion of a requested record after removing or redacting those portions claimed to be exempt, explain in writing the justification for redacting the record, indicate the extent of any redactions on the portion of the record which is made available or published and where technically feasible indicate on the redacted portion itself the specific exemption(s) claimed.

Thank for the work FBI does every day, and thank you for the bureau's commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
